result:
I've saved the Q3 analysis to `/work/answer.json`. Run with the same method on Q2, the script reproduces all 10 of the reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net sales | consumer, 288,339,834 won |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 244 |
| c. Category with highest net sales | svc, 312,178,057 won |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the most refunds | u106@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 230 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 695,232 won |
| h. September vs. August growth | 1.9% |

The data isn't clean, so I had to make three interpretations. All three were needed to get the Q2 reference values back:

- **Order dates:** I counted dates in Korean time (UTC+9). The stored times are in UTC, and with UTC the Q2 numbers don't match the reference.
- **Text cleanup:** I trimmed spaces and ignored case in segment, category and status values. For example, "Enterprise " and "enterprise" count as the same segment.
- **Counting customers:** In b and f, I counted a customer as one email address rather than one customer record. The DB has 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails. Counted by record, Q2 gives 287 instead of 241.

STATUS: DONE
